name: slack
description: Slack as a door to the Hive: the person writes in a DM with the Hive's Slack app or a channel for the lead, a channel per project lead, or `to <agent>: …` for any running agent, and the answers come back in the same Slack thread (a Slack thread is one chat thread; the lead reads the lines as `Module slack: …`). It keeps its own Slack channels, private, one per project or shared by several: a lead's line `slack: channel <name> [lead] [project …]` (written to the person with hive agent message; also `slack: drop <project>`, `slack: archive <name>`, `slack: channels`) makes or takes the channel, invites the person and the project's own users and maps it, answered in the same thread; a retired project's channel is archived once empty. The map is in its state, so slack.json needs only the tokens and the people. It connects over Socket Mode, outbound only, so no port opens on this machine. The Slack app and its tokens are the person's: docs/README.md gives the app's manifest (slack-app.json) and where the tokens go, slack.json in the module's own HOME (.hive/modules/slack/, covered from every agent's sandbox), read only by this program. It carries in messages only from the Slack users slack.json names, and from each project's own users (slack.json or the project's exported <name>.dispatch.json side file), who reach only that project's lead from its channel. `run` builds it once with the Go on PATH or the Hive's own (GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off: nothing fetched).
